chapter_theme: The three forms (முச்சொரூபம்): the soul rises past the impurities into the knowledge of 'I am Siva' and release in three forms, while the Lord, beyond measure, becomes formless, form and both, comes as Shakti and guru, and holds the three forms as a gem holds its lustre.
structure_note: 2478 to 2481 describe the three forms and the Lord in and beyond them; 2482 and 2483 use the gem and its light; 2484 turns to a yogic instruction.

2478.reading: Rising stage by stage past the five impurities, reaching the stilled knowledge of 'I am Siva', and gaining release in the three forms as if they were separate, at the end the ancient Supreme makes the truth plain.
2478.nuance: மலம் ஐந்து are traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and tirodhana. வேறும் என, 'as if separate', suggests the three forms are distinguished only on the way.

2479.reading: Three mansions are the seat of the three; in the three the thirty-six arise; on seeing the light that sprouts and rises within the three, the body's reckoning ceases.
2479.nuance: The three mansions may be the three bodies (gross, subtle, causal) or three regions of the yogic body; the three who dwell there are traditionally Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra. காயக் கணக்கு, the body's account, may be its debts of deeds.

2480.reading: When the world is moved from its place and the ages are gone, and the three abiding lights become one, who can know the measure and greatness of the Lord within the many things and their natures?
2480.nuance: The three lights are traditionally sun, moon and fire. The verse sets the Lord against dissolution: when all else merges, he remains past measure.

2481.reading: Dividing the distinctions that start from the great one, the Lord becomes formless, form and form-and-formless; comes as Shakti, as guru, as the many souls; and dwelling with them in form, is one with them and not one.
2481.nuance: பெருவாய் may be mahat, the great principle, or something else. ஒன்றாய் அன்றாம், one and not one, states the relation of Lord and souls as Siddhanta takes it.

2482.reading: As a gem's light and lustre are its own marks and it stands as the gem, so the gentle three forms and the Shaktis rest in him: hold to the feet of great Nandi who made them serve.
2482.nuance: The gem and its light is the classic image of a quality inseparable from what has it. பணிவித்த, who made them bow or serve, may also mean who made me bow.

2483.reading: As one good gem holds its stone-light, colour, lustre and the strike of its rays, so in the three voids where words cease, speaking the great word beyond speech, is the experience at the end of the three, free of darkness.
2483.nuance: நாடி ஒண் முப்பதும் is obscure (perhaps the bright thirty, or a misreading of முப்பதம், the three padas), as is முத்திராந்தம், the end of the mudras or of the three. The gem image continues 2482.

2484.reading: Restrain the nada of the moving red lotus that holds a light within, and open from above the doorway that she who holds the waters has sealed shut.
2484.nuance: The red lotus is a centre of the yogic body. பயோதரி, she who holds water or milk, is taken as kundalini or a nadi that blocks the way up; விடம் may be 'place' or 'poison'. A plain reading is not available.

links.note: Both use a gem whose light, lustre and rays belong to it: 2482 for the three forms resting in the Lord, 2483 for the experience in the three voids.

source_issues: 2483 line 2 (நாடிஒண் முப்பதும்) is obscure; முப்பதும் may be a misreading of முப்பதம்.
